NgraceChangeDesignContext.Rationale:
RM-PILOT-APPROVAL review.md:80 wants "a number, per bundle, in the ledger". Read as a stored field, that would be a new record. F134.2 and D21 reject a new record when the existing data already answers the question. The Decision list is the ledger; the Replacement pointers are the supersede graph. Deriving the two numbers and surfacing them is the reading that keeps both sentences: the ledger is the source, not a new home.
Two numbers, not one. A re-ratification counter on today's archive is 0 everywhere, because amendments still happen while draft. That is the after instrument, live the moment a second fingerprinted approve lands. Supersede-chain depth is the before instrument: eight discarded bundles, two of them two-step chains, three from one session. Reporting only re-ratifications would give pilot nothing to compare against, which is why these instrument bundles were ordered before scheduling pilot.
Transitions, not distinct-set-minus-one. The brief wrote both formulas. Set cardinality undercounts A→B→A (revert to a previously ratified byte state). "A re-approval whose fingerprint differs" is the event the budget will later consume. No-op re-approve (identical fingerprint) still adds 0 under either formula.
Chain depth accumulates; re-ratifications do not. Pilot's budget is per bundle, so a replacement starts at 0 re-ratifications. A chain is the current regime's accumulated cost of getting one surviving work item, so the tip of SENTINEL→IDENTITY→RESOLVER reports 2. A reader of the survivor who saw only 1 would miss the two-step. Local 0/1 is recoverable from accumulated depth on a linear chain; the reverse is not.
Surfaces: status --json is the machine archive (already lists applied and superseded bundles). That is the close/archive record without writing a new file into the bundle. Review --change is constraint 5 of the pilot note ("surfaced at close and in review") and follows the attempt-pair not-run honesty bar. Status text prints only non-zero, like orphans=, so 57 zero lines do not drown the signal. No new review.* code: a historical supersede is not a finding.
Unfingerprinted Decisions (42 of 55) are excluded, not guessed. C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE's two unnamed permits were byte-identical (F40); counting permit-minus-one would have called that an amendment. They must read 0.

Alternatives.Alternative: Store an incrementing count attribute on each approve Decision, or a new ledger section. Makes the number "in the ledger" literally. Rejected: the history already encodes it, and F134.2 rejected a new kind on that ground. A stored field can drift from the Decisions it claims to summarise.
Report only re-ratifications. Smaller surface. Rejected: it reads 0 on all 51 ledgers and gives pilot no before. The brief asked for both.

Report only supersede-chain depth. Reads history now. Rejected: the moment pilot ships, supersede stops being the amendment equivalent, and the counter would go dark just as the thing it was built to measure starts.

Distinct fingerprints minus one, as the brief's formula line. Cheaper, order-free. Rejected: A then B then A is two re-ratifications, one distinct extra. The event the budget will consume is the transition.

Do not inherit chain depth; each replacement reports 1. Matches per-bundle budget symmetry. Rejected: status is per-change, and the consumer looking at the surviving tip would see 1 for a two-step chain. The before/after comparison is "what did this work item cost", which is accumulated. Re-ratifications stay per-bundle to keep the budget semantics.

Inherit re-ratifications along the chain as well. One accumulated cost number. Rejected: mixing a discarded bundle's (today always 0) post-approval count into the survivor would poison the per-bundle budget the moment both numbers are non-zero.
Omit the JSON keys when 0, like orphanCount. Smaller payloads. Rejected: this instrument's zero is a measured zero, and omission is how "not implemented" currently looks. Always present as numbers.

Add a review.* finding when either count is greater than 0. Loud, like a supersede. Rejected: the eight superseded bundles are history, not defects. A finding would fail close on every chain survivor.

Print the counts on ngrace gate archive stdout only. Matches "at close" literally. Rejected: archive already moves the bundle into the status archive list, and stdout is not how anyone tallies 51 bundles.

Teach the numbers in ngrace-status must_report. Agents would see them. Rejected: the consumer is the maintainer deciding pilot, not an executing agent, and a skill edit moves skillTextLines totalBytes off 58931 (F133 / four prior bundles).

DeferredDecisions.Decision: Effort accounting. Next instrument bundle. Prefer WriteEvidence digest churn over self-reported tokens.
Whether an exhausted amendment budget refuses or pauses. RM-PILOT-APPROVAL open question; this bundle does not budget.

Scenarios.Scenario: This repository, after the change. status --json: every change has both keys; reRatificationCount is 0 everywhere; C-CURSOR-TASK-RESOLVER and C-LINT-PHASE-HONESTY-2 report supersedeChainDepth 2; origins of chains report 0.
Throwaway, two gate approve runs, no byte change. Two Decision entries, same fingerprint. reRatificationCount 0. The no-op must not inflate.
Throwaway, spec edited and re-approved so fingerprint differs. reRatificationCount 1. Discrimination against the no-op.
Historical shape: two unnamed unfingerprinted approve permits (C-EXPLAIN-COVERAGE / F40). reRatificationCount 0.
First spec approve then first plan approve. Two artifacts, two baselines, count 0.
Fingerprinted spec permits A, then B, then A. reRatificationCount 2.
ngrace review with no --change. Amendment count line is not-run and names --change. With --change, ran, including zeros.
